sections.h2: Selling a house in Riviera Beach
sections.html:
Waterfront living defines Riviera Beach, a compact Palm Beach County city of about 39,357 people as of July 2025. The Port of Palm Beach lies inside its limits, and the city covers both the mainland and part of Singer Island. A seller typically picks from three routes.

  • Hire an agent and wait for a conventional buyer.
  • Find your own buyer and sell directly.
  • Take a cash offer for the house in its current state, closing when you choose.

Lots, ages and styles are mixed, so the condition of the house and its exact location drive the price more than any citywide number.

In this dense city, 62.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, so almost two in five households rent. Lease and deposit records are worth keeping ready, because many houses change hands with a tenant inside.

sections.h2: Palm Beach County homestead rules for sellers
sections.html:
The first layer of a homestead exempts $25,000 of the opening $50,000 of assessed value from every tax. A second layer skips school taxes and tops out at $25,722 for 2025. Your January 1 status decides eligibility, and the application is due by March 1.

The office renews exemptions each year without a new form and mails a receipt card at the end of December. If you sell, or if marriage, divorce, death or a change in use alters ownership, tell the property appraiser by phone or email. A buyer starts with a new application.

Save Our Homes limits yearly growth in assessed value to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is smaller, and after a sale the property goes back to just value. Amendment 3 won approval on November 3, 2026, and the Palm Beach office can explain the larger exemption that starts in 2027.

You can file online through E File, at one of five service centers or by mail, and ownership-change calls go to 561.355.2866. Have Social Security numbers for every owner and spouse, a Florida driver's license and a second proof of residence ready.

  • Report a move-out so the exemption ends cleanly.
  • Ask about portability if you are buying another Florida homestead.

An unpaid bill is delinquent from April 1. The county tax collector then auctions a certificate on it, no later than June 1, to the investor willing to take the lowest interest rate (section 197.432). Bids drop in quarter-percent steps.

The investor holding the certificate can start a tax deed case once two years run from April 1 of the issuance year, with a $75 fee (section 197.502). On a homestead, one-half of the latest assessed value gets added to the opening bid. A public auction follows at the clerk's office. The winner deposits the larger of 5 percent or $200 and has 24 hours, not counting weekends and holidays, to pay the rest.

A certificate on your house is a reason to sell before the deed process begins, because that can protect your remaining equity. Get the redemption total from the Palm Beach tax collector rather than guessing.

To end a month-to-month tenancy, a landlord must give at least 30 days' notice ahead of the end of a monthly period (section 83.57). Once a court enters judgment, the sheriff posts 24 hours' notice before carrying out the writ (section 83.62).

Stamp tax on the deed runs 70 cents for each $100, and the clerk collects it when recording. Everyone who signs is liable for it. The recording fee under section 28.24 is $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional one, plus technology charges.

  • Have the closing agent calculate lien payoffs and the tax proration.
  • Collect leases and deposit records to pass to the buyer.
  • Line up the two witnesses the deed needs.

sections.h2: Selling with tenants in the house
sections.html:
Selling does not cancel a lease. A tenant with time left stays unless a lawful notice or an agreement ends the tenancy, and the buyer takes the house with that lease. Let the tenant know in writing that a sale is coming, and schedule showings at reasonable hours with notice.

A buyer who wants the house empty should say so early. Some cash buyers will wait for the lease to end or pay for a move-out, and either arrangement belongs in the contract. Back rent is handled at closing, and your title agent can show you how. Pass along the lease, the deposit amount and any management agreement so nothing surprises the buyer.

Compare the rent actually paid with the lease before you sign. A cash buyer may lower the price for a below-market rent, and a buyer planning to live there may ask for the house vacant.

sections.h2: Marketing a house near the port or Singer Island
sections.html:
It does. The port is part of the waterfront identity, and the waterfront marketplace draws visitors headed for the cruise ships. Houses near the water or the marinas are judged on views, boat access and insurance costs. Inland houses are judged on lot size, roof age and distance to the bridges.

Seasonal storms shape how buyers look at a coastal city. Expect questions about the roof, shutters or impact windows, and the date of your last insurance claim. If you replaced anything after a storm, keep the permit and the final inspection record, since a buyer's insurer may ask for them before binding coverage.

Pull your flood zone information, insurance policy and permit records together before you talk price, so a buyer can weigh ongoing costs as well as the sale price. Sellers who document these early usually face fewer renegotiation requests after inspection.

1. Give the buyer the address, your mortgage balance and the names of occupants.
  2. Study the written offer for price, repair terms and closing day.
  3. The title agent searches the record and orders payoff letters.
  4. Sign the deed with two witnesses watching.
  5. The clerk records it, then your proceeds are released.

Prepare a payoff letter, your newest tax bill, any lease and your insurance declarations page before the first call. Then put three questions to each buyer: how long the offer lasts, who pays for the title policy, and whether an inspection can change the price. Write down the answers.

On the day of the closing, plan to bring a photo ID, review the settlement statement line by line and sign the deed in front of the two witnesses. Leave keys, garage openers and any gate cards with the closing agent. Once the clerk records the deed, the transfer is done and your money is released. Hold on to every page you signed, because the property appraiser or your own tax preparer may ask for them later.

Since nobody is waiting on a lender's appraisal, title work sets the speed of a cash sale. Store the signed settlement statement and recorded deed with your tax records.

faqs.q: Is a tenant-occupied Riviera Beach house sellable?
faqs.a: Yes. Until its term runs out or proper notice ends it, the lease stays in force, so give the title agent the lease, deposit records and any management agreement.

faqs.q: Does the buyer keep my Palm Beach homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. Your buyer must apply separately, and you should tell the property appraiser about the sale.

faqs.q: What is the stamp tax rate on a Riviera Beach deed?
faqs.a: The state rate of 70 cents per $100 of consideration, which applies everywhere but Miami-Dade, with all parties to the document liable.

faqs.q: When do unpaid property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Certificates on unpaid items are offered for sale by June 1.

faqs.q: Is a cash sale quicker than listing here?
faqs.a: Usually, because no bank appraisal is required. Clear title, a witnessed deed and recording still come before funds.
